LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 8.3.1 SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are some of your school rules?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text
2. use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: GRAMMAR IN USE 8.3.1 SENTENCES
This lesson teaches Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences for Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences above.
2. Explain Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences important for a Grade 5 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are some of your school rules?
2. How do you give instructions?
3. Why do we ask questions?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text
2. use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
